issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B: Start, Union, and Width interval operators.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe showed Python/native-loaded intervalUnion widened finite open boundaries for downstream intervalContains and intervalStart.
issues.root_cause: Python intervalUnion selected effective bounds for comparison but serialized authored raw open bounds; C++ union output was also normalized to the same canonical effective-bound shape for parity.
issues.resolution: Python intervalUnion and C++ Interval::union_of now serialize canonical effective Start/End boundaries.
issues.verified_in: python3 .temp/qa/cql17_explorer_probe.py; interval part3 pytest; native C++ cql unittest; full conformance; full pytest

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B: Decimal minimum step size, Point From, Size, Start, and Width.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe showed no-Python C++ decimal open Start/End and pointFrom diverged from forced Python fallback, and decimal Width/Size did not consistently use effective endpoints.
issues.root_cause: Decimal successor/predecessor formatting and interval Width/Size calculations did not consistently preserve CQL scale-8 effective endpoints.
issues.resolution: Python and C++ decimal interval helpers now use scale-8 successor/predecessor behavior for Start, End, pointFrom, Width, and Size.
issues.verified_in: python3 .temp/qa/cql17_explorer_probe.py; interval part3 pytest; native C++ cql unittest; full conformance; full pytest

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B: Contains/In and Union interval operators.
issues.evidence: Translated `0 in (Interval(0, 3] union Interval[1, 6])` emitted SQL IN against an interval-valued function and binder-failed.
issues.root_cause: _translate_in_op only recognized literal interval right operands, not interval-valued set-operation expressions.
issues.resolution: The translator now routes interval-valued right operands through intervalContains.
issues.verified_in: interval part3 pytest; full conformance; full pytest

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B: Width and Quantity unit-aware interval semantics.
issues.evidence: Architect probe showed no-Python C++ intervalWidth over Interval[1 'g', 2000 'mg'] returned 1999 g while Python/native returned 1 g.
issues.root_cause: C++ Quantity interval Width/Size subtracted raw magnitudes without converting the high bound to the low bound unit.
issues.resolution: C++ Quantity interval Width/Size now converts high-bound units into the low-bound unit before subtraction.
issues.verified_in: python3 .temp/qa/cql17_explorer_probe.py; interval part3 pytest; native C++ cql unittest; full conformance; full pytest
